seo.description: An AI agent workspace for recruiters to clarify hiring needs, organize candidate evidence, prepare interviews, coordinate feedback, and draft status updates.

hero.eyebrow: A configurable AI workspace for real work
hero.title: An AI agent workspace for recruiters and talent teams
hero.description: Structure hiring intake, candidate evidence, interview preparation, and status communication in a human-controlled AI workspace for recruiting teams.

burdens.eyebrow: The repetitive work around the profession
burdens.title: recruiters and talent teams should not spend their best hours rebuilding context.
burdens.description: Hiring slows down when the role, evidence, interview criteria, and candidate communication are rebuilt by different people at every stage.

items.label: Context
items.title: Job requirements begin ambiguous
items.description: A job title can hide conflicting expectations about outcomes, seniority, constraints, and what success should look like.

items.label: Format
items.title: Candidate context is repeatedly reconstructed
items.description: Recruiters and interviewers repeatedly turn résumés, notes, portfolios, and correspondence into their own partial summaries.

items.label: Coordination
items.title: Interview evidence arrives in different formats
items.description: Scorecards, free-form notes, and delayed feedback make it difficult to compare evidence against the agreed role criteria.

items.label: Continuity
items.title: Status communication consumes focus
items.description: Scheduling changes, interviewer reminders, candidate updates, and debrief follow-ups compete with actual recruiting judgment.

buildingBlocks.title: Compose the workflow from practical building blocks.
buildingBlocks.description: Floatboat does not prescribe one professional method. It follows the materials, standards, and approval points you select.

items.example: Start from approved files, records, and sources rather than an empty prompt.
Classify material, normalize names, and identify missing inputs.
Pull facts, dates, data, claims, and open questions.
Contrast versions, standards, periods, or alternatives.
items.result: A focused list of changes and differences.

items.example: Turn approved material into briefs, outlines, tables, and drafts.
Save proven steps, formats, and approval points.
items.result: A reusable workflow shaped by the team.

workflows.title: Start from real assignments, not a fixed professional playbook.
workflows.description: Each workflow begins with material and rules you control, returns an inspectable result, and stops before professional judgment.

items.title: Turn intake into a role brief
items.job: Consolidate business need, outcomes, constraints, and interview criteria before sourcing begins.
items.output: A shared role brief and structured scorecard draft.
items.boundary: The hiring team sets lawful criteria and approves the role requirements.

items.title: Prepare a candidate evidence packet
items.job: Organize candidate-provided material against approved, job-related criteria for human review.
items.output: A source-linked packet with evidence and interview questions.
items.boundary: People—not the system—assess candidates and make employment decisions.

items.title: Coordinate interviews and follow-up
items.job: Create interviewer briefs, consolidate notes, and draft timely candidate communications.
items.output: Interview packs, debrief summary, and editable status messages.
items.boundary: Recruiters approve communications and protect sensitive candidate information.

boundaries.title: Automate preparation, not professional responsibility.
boundaries.description: The useful boundary is between preparing an inspectable work product and making a consequential professional decision.
assists: Source indexes, context briefs, and evidence maps
Comparisons, extracted fields, and open questions
Meeting packs, status summaries, and communication drafts
Grounded outlines, reports, and editable first drafts
retains: Verification of facts, data, and sources
Approval for every external publication, submission, or consequential action
boundaries.note: Floatboat is a general-purpose Agent Workspace. It does not replace professional qualification, legal responsibility, or organizational governance. Data handling depends on the models, tools, connectors, permissions, and policies selected for the workspace.

faq.title: AI workspace questions for recruiters and talent teams
faq.description: Recruiting automation must improve preparation without turning incomplete evidence into a hiring decision or weakening candidate privacy.

items.question: Is Floatboat an ATS or candidate-ranking system?
items.answer: No. Your ATS remains the hiring system of record. Floatboat helps prepare role briefs, interview materials, evidence summaries, and communication drafts around the information your team is permitted to use.

items.question: Can it screen out or rank candidates automatically?
items.answer: That is not the intended workflow. It can organize job-related evidence against approved criteria, but recruiters and hiring managers must evaluate people, investigate gaps, and make employment decisions.

items.question: Can it use our role brief and interview scorecard?
items.answer: Yes. Define outcomes, required evidence, legal constraints, question areas, and the scorecard format before candidate preparation begins.

items.question: How do we prevent invented candidate claims?
items.answer: Limit summaries to candidate-provided or approved sources, preserve links to the original evidence, label missing information as unknown, and require a recruiter to verify every claim used in an interview brief.

items.question: What candidate information belongs in the workspace?
items.answer: Only job-relevant information that policy and applicable law permit the team to process. Avoid unnecessary sensitive attributes, keep access narrow, and review the data practices of each model and connector.

items.question: Can it contact candidates or schedule interviews without review?
items.answer: It can prepare messages and scheduling options, but a responsible recruiter should confirm recipients, availability, wording, and stage before any candidate-facing action.

items.question: What is the safest first recruiting workflow?
items.answer: Start with an approved role brief and scorecard, then generate an interviewer packet for one candidate. Check every statement against the source material before deciding whether to reuse the process.

finalCta.title: Give the repetitive preparation around recruiters and talent teams a better workspace.
finalCta.description: Begin with one approved role brief and a structured interview packet. Reduce preparation time without handing candidate judgment to the system.
